draft.title: Cultural determinants of wellbeing
card: Cultural determinants are parts of culture and community that support the social and emotional wellbeing of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. They are strengths that help wellbeing, not only risks to avoid.
communities having the right and the power to make decisions about matters that affect their own lives, services and futures.
links to culture, Country and community, such as language, kinship, ceremony, stories and time spent on Country. These links support a strong sense of identity and belonging.
When services are designed and led by community members, they can better fit the needs and values of that community. This can support wellbeing.
draft.remember: Self-determination and strong connection to culture, Country and community support wellbeing.

a.q: Which example best shows self-determination in a community?
opts: An Aboriginal community controls the health service it uses
A government office plans a health service for a community
A hospital runs a cultural awareness day for its staff
A school teaches students about a community's history
a.why: Self-determination means a community has the power to make decisions about matters that affect it. A community controlling its own health service is an example. A government office planning the service for the community is tempting, but the decisions are made by others.

b.q: A Torres Strait Islander teenager moves to a large city for school and is cut off from family, language and island life. Which idea best explains why this may affect their wellbeing?
opts: Strong links to culture and Country can support wellbeing
Living in a city always causes a mental health disorder
Wellbeing depends only on how well a student does at school
Self-determination means a teenager must live at home
b.why: Being cut off from family, language and Country removes connections that support social and emotional wellbeing. It may weaken that support, not guarantee a disorder. The option about a city always causing a disorder is wrong because the card says connection can support wellbeing, not that its loss always harms.
b.clue: Look at what the teenager has lost contact with.

a.best: An Aboriginal community controls the health service it uses

b.best: Strong links to culture and Country can support wellbeing

problems.detail: The right option is the only one that is hedged ('can support'). Every distractor uses an absolute ('only', 'always', 'must') and is plainly extreme, so a student can pick the answer by test-taking logic without knowing the idea. The distractors should be plausible and similarly worded.

opts: An Aboriginal community controls the health service it uses
A government office plans a health service for a community
A hospital runs a cultural awareness day for its staff
A school teaches students about a community's history
a.why: Self-determination means a community has the power to make decisions about matters that affect it. A community controlling its own health service is an example. A government office planning the service for the community is tempting, but the decisions are made by others.

b.q: With family support, a Torres Strait Islander teenager moves to a large city for school. There, they are cut off from kin, language and island life. Which cultural determinant has been weakened?
opts: Connection to culture, Country and community
The community's power to make its own decisions
Community control of local health services
Community-led design of school programs
b.why: The teenager has lost contact with kin, language and Country, which are forms of connection that support identity and belonging. The other three options describe self-determination, a community's power over its decisions and services. Nothing in the case takes that power away from the community, so those options do not fit.
b.clue: Compare what the teenager has lost with each definition on the card.
